title: Good Quality Heater- Not as good as I was hoping
text:
Good Quality Heater- Not as good as I was hoping. When my two 21 year old ceramic heaters started showing signs of failing I started hunting for new ones. After a long and arduous search I decided to give this one a try. I am very glad I did. We have a living room that is about 400 sq ft. that opens to both a sun room and the kitchen, about 900 sq ft total. This heater was able to keep the entire area in the upper 60s when it was below freezing outside, no sunshine. It took 1 hour to heat this area from 58 to 68. I do believe if this was utilized in a closed area of 400 to 500 sq ft., it would be more than adequate.

The construction is pure and simple. It uses a small blower similar to what is used in your furnace to distribute the heat. It is much quieter than fan driven heaters, has a higher cfm (cubic feet per minute) output and the delivery of the heat is very warm, and "softer" than fan driven models. It tends to make a sizable area around it feel cozy as best as I can describe it. When plugged in and turned on high it doesn't seem to have any more loading on the circuit than a standard hair dryer. It is much more efficient in producing and distributing 1500W worth of heating than anything I've ever seen.

The unit does remain cool to the touch except one small area above the heater core on top where you might describe it as barely warm. The filter on the back is basically a hair screen, not a dust filter. The power cord is 6 foot long, adequately sized, with a standard 3 prong outlet connection. The casters are adequate for hard flooring, not carpet. But the unit itself does not feel like it is over 20 lbs. to me. The remote is cute.

I'll be curious to see the electric bill. We are now successfully using this one 1500W heater to warm the same area it required two 1500W ceramics to heat previously. My only last concern would be with longevity. With a 3 year warranty I expect with normal care and maintenance (cleanings) this heater should be around a long time. I will update if I run into any problems.

UPDATE 2-17-2014: This unit is now failing. It still produces heat on the Lo setting, but produces much less on the Hi side then when new. Now the high and low side are producing an equal amount of heat. The unit has been subjected to no rough handling whatsoever. The filter has been cleaned exactly as recommended. I can only conclude that something inside the unit has failed. Considering this unit has a 3 year warranty and has displayed a failure within 4 months is quite irritating. I will be inquiring how much this would cost me to ship it back to the manufacturer for repairs, but no matter what the cost I find failure within this short of a time span pathetic, thus I have revised my rating on this product. With this kind of performance I could NOT RECOMMEND purchasing this product based on longevity.
